messages:
noah: Hey team, first-day setup question. I pulled the repo and ran `docker compose up` but the db crashes during init. app logs show `FATAL: invalid value for parameter \"lc_collate\": \"en_US.UTF-8\"` and the container exits. Postgres image is `postgres:15-alpine` and I'm on an M1 Mac.

olivia: welcome! that error usually means the container doesn't have the requested locale available. alpine images often don't include glibc locales. did you bind-mount a host `./pgdata` dir?

noah: yes I mounted `./pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data` so the data dir persisted. tried removing it and restarting but same error. here's the end of the logs:

noah: ```
2026-03-10 08:12:34.123 UTC [1] FATAL: invalid value for parameter "lc_collate": "en_US.UTF-8"
2026-03-10 08:12:34.124 UTC [1] HINT: The available collations are: C, POSIX
```

ryan: yup that's alpine. Two options: 1) switch to a Debian-based image (e.g. `postgres:15-bullseye`) which has the locales, or 2) build a custom image that installs `glibc-locales`/`locales` and generates `en_US.UTF-8` before initdb runs.

noah: switching to `postgres:15-bullseye` fixed the locale error, thanks. but now I hit a permission error when using the host mount: `could not create directory \"pg_wal\": Permission denied`.

olivia: classic mac bind-mount/uid mapping issue. On macOS the host UID may not match the postgres UID in the container. For dev, easiest fixes are:
- use a named volume (no host bind) so Docker/compose manages permissions
- chown the host folder to uid 999 (`sudo chown -R 999:999 ./pgdata`) and restart
- if you want host files visible, use `:delegated` mount and `post-start` script to fix perms (annoying)

noah: I tried named volume and rebuild, postgres comes up and migrations run. final note: I had `image: postgres:15-alpine` in our compose sample in the README; maybe we should recommend `postgres:15-bullseye` for Mac users or add a note about locales and bind mounts.

infra-bot: Heads-up: dev-setup doc updated with a short section: "Prefer Debian-based Postgres images (e.g., postgres:15-bullseye) for local mac dev to avoid missing locales; prefer named volumes over bind-mounting ./pgdata. For mac M1, if using bind mounts chown to 999:999." https://go.redwood/dev-setup (:book:)

noah: adding that to my onboarding notes and pinging @olivia to update quickstart. Really appreciate the help! :tada:
